title: 全球7.4亿人：耳朵里在响，你身边有患者吗？
speaker: Bloomberg

segments.en: We live in a world where loud is equated with fun, but for hundreds of millions of people, they're paying a high price for that. They have tonight us.
segments.zh: 我们生活在一个把大声等同于有趣的世界，但数亿人正为此付出高昂代价。今晚，他们就在我们身边。

segments.en: Bloomberg Pursuit staff writer Hannah Elliott warns that someone you know has it and that it's a ticking time bomb. That's right. And I just fire alarms here in the studio. In the United States,
segments.zh: 彭博 Pursuit 特约撰稿人 Hannah Elliott 警告说，你认识的人中可能就有人患有此症，它就像一颗定时炸弹。没错，我在演播室里就听到了火警声。在美国，

segments.en: the American Tennis Foundation says over 50 million people are suffering. That's 15 percent of the population. And it's so bad for about two million Americans. They're actually debilitated by it.
segments.zh: 美国网球基金会称，超过5000万人受此困扰，占总人口的15%。其中约200万美国人情况严重，甚至因此丧失行动能力。

segments.en: Veterans, musicians, people who love concerts and motor sports are all in an increased risk. And for Hannah, writing the story was deeply personal. My husband has it. And the funny thing is my
segments.zh: 退伍军人、音乐人、以及热爱音乐会和赛车运动的人群风险更高。对 Hannah 来说，撰写这篇报道感触颇深。我丈夫就有此症。有趣的是，

segments.en: husband's a car guy. And as you know, my day job is mostly writing about cars in the car world.
segments.zh: 我丈夫是个车迷。而你知道，我的日常工作主要是报道汽车和汽车界。

segments.en: And I started to realize that when you're in a group of car people, if you the minute you mentioned tonight us, everyone starts to come out of the woodwork and says, I have it or my buddy has it or
segments.zh: 我开始意识到，当你和一群车迷在一起时，只要一提耳鸣，大家就会纷纷站出来说，我有，或者我朋友有，

segments.en: my brother has it or my dad has it. And I just started to realize, oh, in this tiny segment of car people, it's very prevalent. And then it started to spill out into, oh, my motorcycle friends talk
segments.zh: 我兄弟有，我爸爸有。我开始意识到，哦，在车迷这个小圈子里，它非常普遍。然后我发现，我的摩托车友也在谈论，

segments.en: about it. Oh, my musician friends talk about it. And it became this thing where it's like, wow, this seems to be very common. But no one's really talking about it because some people can kind of
segments.zh: 我的音乐人朋友也在谈论。这让我觉得，哇，这似乎非常普遍。但没人真正谈论它，因为有些人能忍受，

segments.en: live with it. And others don't want to talk about it because it's so frustrating that there's no cure. So they don't talk about it at all. And it just got me very, very curious about what's really
segments.zh: 而另一些人则不愿提及，因为无药可治令人沮丧。所以他们干脆闭口不谈。这让我非常好奇，到底真相如何。
